classification.difficultyReason: Use right-triangle cosine, recognise that the congruent tangent triangles double the calculated angle to give the minor central angle, then calculate the minor arc and subtract it from the circumference for the major arc.

content.prompt: $AC$ and $AD$ are equal tangents to the circle of radius $5$ cm. The point $A$ is $13$ cm from the centre $B$. Note that $BC$ is perpendicular to $AC$ and $BD$ is perpendicular to $AD$.

spec.description: Circle at left with centre B, external point A at right, upper and lower tangents AC and AD, radii BC and BD, and horizontal BA labelled 13. All four named points are marked. Right-angle squares are constructed from the actual tangent and radius directions.
spec.mathematics: BA = 13 cm, BC = BD = 5 cm, AC perpendicular to BC and AD perpendicular to BD. Coordinates derive the tangent points from these givens; the minor arc CD faces A.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated angle or arc length displayed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate $\angle ABC$ in radians, correct to three decimal places.

answer.worked:
In right-angled $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{BC}{BA}\\\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{5}{13}\\\angle ABC&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\\angle ABC&\approx1.176\text{ radians}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the length of the minor arc $CD$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
The right triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are congruent: they share hypotenuse $AB$ and have equal radii $BC$ and $BD$. Hence $\angle CBD=2\angle ABC$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta_{\text{minor}}&=2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\l_{\text{minor}}&=r\theta_{\text{minor}}\\l_{\text{minor}}&=5\left[2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\right]\\l_{\text{minor}}&\approx11.76\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the length of the major arc $CD$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Subtract the unrounded minor-arc length from the circumference.

$$\begin{align*}l_{\text{major}}&=2\pi r-l_{\text{minor}}\\l_{\text{major}}&=10\pi-10\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\l_{\text{major}}&\approx19.66\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
